data.name: Shibnath
data.gender_notes: Shibnath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Shib (auspicious, beneficial, propitious) + Nath (lord, master). The name Shibnath carries the meaning “Auspicious or Beneficent Lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Bengali. Parents who choose Shibnath usually hope their child will grow to embody auspicious or beneficent lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: One who brings prosperity and good fortune
data.etymology: Shibnath belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Auspicious or Beneficent Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shibnath total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Shibnath" holds a great cultural significance in Hinduism as it signifies the endless worship towards the supreme deity Shiva. Shiva is considered the lord of the universe, destroyer of evil, and the source of both creation and destruction. The name is commonly used in various Hindu texts and rituals particularly dedicated to Shiva.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Shibnath" represents an unwavering devotion to Lord Shiva. It reminds us of the spiritual power that exists in the universe and the importance of seeking the blessings of the divine to lead a worthy and meaningful life. The name symbolizes the deep sense of reverence and respect for the divine power and the inner purity and piety of the individual bearing the name.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shibnath: God of Auspiciousness and Victory. The name embodies the divine blessings of achieving victory in all endeavors with auspiciousness. It signifies the presence of the divine guide, bestowing success and prosperity.

historical_references.reference: Shibnath Shastri was a famous Hindu scholar, philosopher, and commentator who lived during the 18th century. He is best known for his works on the Hindu scripture, the Bhagavad Gita. His commentary, titled 'Shibnath Bhavarthamrta', is considered an authoritative interpretation of the text.

Shibnath Sikdar was a freedom fighter and revolutionary leader who played a significant role in the Indian independence movement during the early 20th century. He was a member of the revolutionary organization, 'Deshbandhu Samiti', and was involved in various acts of rebellion against the British colonial rule. He was arrested and hanged by the British authorities in 1923.
